title: ds4: `DS4_RING_MB=128` instead of the default 400 reads prompts 6-12 % faster on 2x 64 GB cards (and leaves ~33 more experts a card in VRAM). Should the prompt ring be sized by VRAM / link speed?
body:
**Platform-specific:** we measured this on one rig only: 2x CMP 170HX 64 GB, card 1 on PCIe Gen2 x4. The gain may come
from the slow link. This is a finding with a question, not a patch.

## Finding

The prompt flow's expert ring is a fixed `DS4_RING_MB` (default 400) of slots in `Chunk::kParts` batches, allocated on
each flow device before expert placement (`ds4_model.cu:4287-4292` in v1.1.34). Unchanged in v1.1.35 per its release
notes, which list no DeepSeek changes; not checked in source. At ~8.8-9 MB an expert blob, 400 MiB is roughly 48
slots, and 128 MiB is 16, still in 4 batches.

Setting `DS4_RING_MB=128` made every prompt length faster in all our arms. The 272 MiB a card it frees also goes to the
experts at placement: 6811 vs 6775 experts in VRAM on CUDA0, 6762 vs 6731 on CUDA1.

## Measured

**Hardware:** 2x CMP 170HX 64 GB (sm_80, CUDA 12.8); card 0 is PCIe Gen2 x16 (6.2 GB/s measured), card 1 Gen2 x4
(1.63 GB/s). Host VM: 16 vCPU Xeon E5-2697 v4 (AVX2), 106 GiB DDR4-2133. Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 GSQ-RCO
IQ2_XXS, layer split, 64K context, `--dspark on`, `--cpu-threads 14`, default `--prefill-chunk`. About 2200 experts
on the CPU lane, so every prompt chunk streams many experts.

**How measured:** Strata's community speed suite through the server (fresh 4K / 16K / 32K prompts, prompt tok/s; an
agent session with prefix reuse, time to first token), plus our own 8K prefill. Each pair runs the same binary and
env; only `DS4_RING_MB` differs.

| build (base) | ring | 4K | 16K | 32K | 8K prefill | agent TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ours on v1.1.29 | 400 | 975.8 | 1567.3 | 1732.8 | 603.1 | 7.90 s |
| | 128 | 1093.6 (+12.1 %) | 1683.4 (+7.4 %) | 1833.8 (+5.8 %) | 650.0 (+7.8 %) | 6.51 s |
| ours on v1.1.29, more patches | 400 | 1000.4 | 1584.6 | 1746.7 | 611.0 | 7.76 s |
| | 128, r1 / r2 | 1119.4 / 1117.9 (+12 %) | 1709.5 / 1701.3 (+7.6 %) | 1858.5 / 1849.7 (+6.1 %) | 652.4 / 652.4 (+6.8 %) | 6.86 / 6.76 s |

- **Decode:** `--dspark none` 24.13 vs 24.28 ms a step (-0.6 %). The DSpark text changes because placement changes, so
  its ms a window is not matched work.
- **Quality and two chats:** 12/12; two chats in flight 67.6 / 65.2 tok/s.
- We have served with 128 since 2026-10-27.

## What we did not isolate

The extra experts alone cannot explain this. ~33 more a card is ~3 % fewer of the ~1100 a card that a chunk
streams. That bounds their share near 3 % on a link-bound card, below the 12 % at 4K. Our own audit estimated well
under 1 % for decode from them. The gain also shrinks with prompt length
(12 % at 4K, 6 % at 32K). That fits a fixed per-chunk or per-layer start-up cost of the larger ring better: for
example, the first batch of ~12 blobs must arrive before compute starts, against ~4. The x4 link makes that wait
longest. This is a guess. We did not run `DS4_FLOW_STATS` on the pair, nor try 128 at a fixed placement.

## Question / proposal

- Is 400 MiB tuned for a specific case (fast links, small cards)? On 64 GB cards with a slow link, 128 is faster at
  every prompt length we tried.
- Options: size the ring from the measured link speed and the blob size (the flow already measures the link). Or
  include `DS4_RING_MB` in `--calibrate`'s prompt tuning. Or simply default to fewer slots where a card's link is
  slow.
- We can run more sizes (64 / 96 / 192 / 256) and a stats pair on this rig if useful.
